shutdown.mon-wed-hour.why: Sleep debt on work nights compounds into exactly the pattern the rest of this fleet exists to break. The curfew is the backstop that makes every other limit survive a bad evening.
shutdown.mon-wed-hour.cost_of_bypass: sudo chattr -i /etc/shutdown-schedule.conf, edit it, and beat guard-file@shutdown-schedule.path to the write. Roughly 90 seconds, and fully logged to /var/log/guard-lib.log.

shutdown.thu-sun-hour.why: Same backstop as the weeknight hour, kept as a separate value so weekends can be tightened or loosened independently of work nights.
shutdown.thu-sun-hour.cost_of_bypass: Identical to shutdown.mon-wed-hour: both live in the same guarded file.

shutdown.morning-end-hour.why: Closes the small-hours window between midnight and the morning, which is where the curfew is easiest to sit out rather than sleep through.
shutdown.morning-end-hour.cost_of_bypass: Same guarded file as the evening hours -- but note this value is NOT currently ratcheted at all: adjust_shutdown_schedule.sh compares only $1 and $2.
shutdown.morning-end-hour.ratchet: LATER only -- and this is the opposite direction from the two evening hours. day-specific-shutdown-check.sh:94 shuts down while the current time is BELOW morning_end_minutes, so a LARGER value means a LONGER shutdown window, i.e. stricter. Writing `-gt` here, as the evening hours do, would ratchet it backwards.
